data.claim: Two causes: (1) PYTHONPATH naming the lane tree leaks into subprocesses that must run installed or sandboxed code, and the guard's own-tree test is cwd-based, so a sandbox cwd reads as foreign; (2) the ci scratch exemption compares the tree's parent to the process's TMPDIR-derived temp root, which the swarm sandbox redirects.
data.falsifier: test_installed_adopt_works_end_to_end passes from a worktree with PYTHONPATH unset (it did) and fails with PYTHONPATH=<worktree> (it did)
data.mechanism: guard_foreign_launch: package imported from linked worktree T, own tree = worktree of cwd; sandbox cwd != T so refuse. Scratch exemption: root.parent == tempfile.gettempdir() which honours TMPDIR.
data.probe_output: unset: 1 passed; PYTHONPATH=worktree: FAILED 'ddflow: imported from the linked worktree .../fix-Bbaaaba1364, not the primary or your own tree; the shared editable install was reset ... re-run the command'. Full suite from the worktree: 254 guard-message hits, all from subprocess cwd!=tree or in-process chdir tests.
data.question: Why does the foreign-launch guard fire from linked worktrees (installed adopt, swarm pilot under ci, pins) and pass on the primary?

evidence.note: research note CONFIRMED: PYTHONPATH leak reproduced (pass unset, fail with PYTHONPATH=worktree); full suite from worktree shows 254 guard refusals, root causes TMPDIR-sensitive scratch exemption, cwd-only own-tree test, in-process chdir

data.context: ci could not pass from a linked worktree: ~250 tests hit the refusal (Bbaaaba1364, Bc28808f9c3, Bdc7cd5b259 and the installed-adopt test).
data.decision: guard_foreign_launch still refuses code imported from a linked worktree that is not the caller's own tree. It now allows exactly two more cases: (1) a ddflow-* scratch tree directly under the process temp root OR /tmp,/var/tmp (ci's tree, even when a test sandbox redirects TMPDIR); (2) a tree the launcher put on PYTHONPATH when the caller's cwd lies outside the primary checkout and all its linked worktrees (a test sandbox, another project). Not excused: a tree reached through the shared editable install (no PYTHONPATH), and any caller inside the checkout family (primary or a lane), PYTHONPATH or not. No environment variable skips the guard. In-process tests stub only the CLI wrapper (tests/conftest.py, marker real_foreign_guard opts back in). pins regenerate refuses to record a guard refusal as a pin and puts the files back. Operator 2026-11-11: fix the guard, no gate skip.
data.title: The foreign-launch guard stays; it excuses only a deliberate PYTHONPATH launch from outside the checkout's family, and ddflow's own scratch trees wherever TMPDIR points

evidence.note: brief --item read; decision D-foreign-launch-explicit-pythonpath recorded; no baseline entries added (env read goes through the Env port, no deferred import)

chunk_findings.detail: The scratch exemption returns before any linked-worktree check, and it keys off the unresolved basename plus the resolved parent. `git worktree add /tmp/ddflow-laneb <lane-b>` (or `ln -s /tmp/real-lane-b /tmp/ddflow-cover` and import through the link) makes `root.name.startswith("ddflow-")` true and `root.resolve().parent` equal `/tmp` or `/var/tmp`, so `foreign_launch_root` returns None and lane B’s unmerged code runs with no refusal. The same happens if `TMPDIR` is the parent of a `ddflow-*` linked worktree: that parent is in `_scratch_parents()`, so the early return treats another lane’s checkout as a scratch tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:foreign_launch_root

chunk_findings.detail: Family membership stops at the nearest `.git` and treats “that tree is not this primary” as outside. From inside lane A, `mkdir -p "$PWD/nest" && mkdir "$PWD/nest/.git" && cd "$PWD/nest"` with `PYTHONPATH` set to lane B (or the primary) makes `in_checkout_family` return False, so `_deliberate_outside_launch` returns OK and lane B’s or the primary’s code runs while the process is still inside this checkout. An empty `.git` directory is enough; it does not have to be a real gitdir.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:in_checkout_family

chunk_findings.detail: `_recorded_a_refusal` treats a regeneration as a foreign-launch refusal whenever any owned file merely contains `FOREIGN_LAUNCH_REFUSAL` as a substring and the command exits 0. It does not compare against the pre-run snapshot, so content that was already there, or a real pin whose legitimate text quotes that message (generated CLI help, a README the recipe owns, a docs tree), is enough. Given a recipe that owns such a file and a regen that exits 0 after updating a different pin, `poisoned` is true, `broke` rolls the good output back, and the pin is marked REFUSED even though no guard refusal was recorded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/pins.py:_records_refusal

chunk_findings.detail: The scratch exemption still returns before any linked-worktree check. It now requires a detached HEAD, but that is not unique to throwaway scratch: `git worktree add --detach /tmp/ddflow-laneb <lane-b-sha>` (or `git worktree add /tmp/ddflow-laneb lane-b && git -C /tmp/ddflow-laneb checkout --detach`) makes the resolved name start with `ddflow-`, the parent a temp dir, and `detached_worktree` true because gitdir `HEAD` is a commit id rather than `ref:`. `_is_scratch_tree` is then true and `foreign_launch_root` returns None, so lane B's unmerged tree runs with no refusal. The branch-only and symlink probes do not cover this; a lane is not pinned to a branch by anything this check reads.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:_is_scratch_tree

chunk_findings.detail: `named_on_pythonpath` treats any ambient `PYTHONPATH` entry as a deliberate launcher choice, and a match plus a cwd outside the checkout family returns OK and skips `repoint_shared_editable`. Given a shared editable install already redirected at `/src/ddflow/.ddflow/worktrees/lane-x`, `PYTHONPATH=/src/ddflow/.ddflow/worktrees/lane-x` left over from an earlier shell, and cwd `[REDACTED:path]` (not under the primary or any linked worktree), the process imports lane-x and the guard now allows it. Before this change that launch was refused and the editable install reset; the persistent env var is not evidence the launcher selected that tree for this run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/guard_launch.py:_deliberate_outside_launch

chunk_findings.detail: A regeneration is treated as clean whenever every owned file that now contains `FOREIGN_LAUNCH_REFUSAL` already contained that byte string in the pre-run snapshot. Given a pin that already quotes the refusal (the docstring explicitly allows that case) and a regen that exits 0 after replacing the file with only the guard refusal, `needle in before` is true, `_recorded_a_refusal` returns false, and the refusal text is kept as the pin instead of rolled back.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/pins.py:_records_refusal

chunk_findings.detail: `test_text_the_pin_already_quoted_is_not_a_recorded_refusal` requires `PN.regenerate` to keep a pin that this run rewrote with `FOREIGN_LAUNCH_REFUSAL` still in it, as long as that phrase was already in `pin.json`. Given `pin.json` already holding `docs: the guard says <FOREIGN_LAUNCH_REFUSAL> X`, the recipe writes that same refusal text plus `more`; the test asserts the run is not a foreign-launch failure and the write is kept. That is the transcript-poison path this change claims to close: a pin that already quotes (or was previously poisoned with) the guard sentence can be regenerated into a new golden that still records `ddflow: imported from the linked worktree ...` and the check will not roll it back.
